title: Some Figures
summary: Over cigars in the lounge, Captain Nemo explains to Aronnax how the Nautilus is built, how it dives, steers and sees, and how he built it in secret. He ends by claiming to be infinitely rich.
details: Captain Nemo spreads out the Nautilus's plans and talks Aronnax through the figures. It is a seventy-meter cylinder with conical ends, built of two steel hulls joined by iron T-bars. Ballast tanks let it sink until it lies flush with the surface. Supplementary tanks take it deeper, and slanting side fins drive it down or up under the propeller's thrust. Because water barely compresses, little extra weight is needed to go deep, and pumps driven by electricity can empty the tanks against great pressure.

A helmsman steers from a pilothouse fitted with thick biconvex glass, and behind it a powerful electric beacon lights the sea for half a mile. Aronnax realizes the beacon explains the mysterious glow of the so-called narwhale. Nemo says ramming the Scotia was an accident. He attacked the Abraham Lincoln only in self-defence and left it able to reach port. He talks of his ship with a father's love: no rigging, no sails, no boilers, no storms below the waves.

Nemo says he studied in London, Paris and New York when he still lived on land. Each part of the Nautilus was ordered from a different maker under a different name, and he and his crew assembled it on a deserted islet, then burned every trace of their stay. With its collections the ship is worth four or five million francs. Asked if he is rich, Nemo says he could pay off France's ten-billion-franc national debt. Aronnax wonders whether he is being made a fool of.

title: The Black Current
summary: Nemo fixes the ship's position off Japan and the voyage officially begins on November 8. Then the lounge panels slide open, and Aronnax, Conseil and Ned Land watch the fish of the Black Current through the windows.
details: At noon the Nautilus surfaces, and from the platform Aronnax sees why it was taken for a sea creature: its plates overlap like reptile scales. Nemo takes the sun's altitude, then works out their position against the Paris meridian, an answer that tells Aronnax nothing about his nationality. They are about 300 miles off Japan, and Nemo declares that the voyage of underwater exploration begins on November 8. He sets a course east-northeast at fifty meters and leaves Aronnax the lounge and its charts.

Alone, Aronnax broods over the captain's hatred of humanity and the hand Nemo never offers. He traces on the map the Kuroshio, or Black Current, the warm ocean river they are about to cross. Ned Land and Conseil arrive and are stunned by the museum-like lounge. Ned wants to know how many crew there are and still talks of escape, calling the ship a sheet-iron prison where they will never see anything.

At that moment the lights go out, panels slide back, and two great windows open onto the sea, lit by the ship's beacon. Conseil lectures Ned on how fish are classified, and Ned rates each order by how good it is to eat. Then the fish arrive, and the two make a perfect naturalist between them: Ned names each fish, Conseil classifies it. Triggerfish, a rare Chinese ray, mackerel, moray eels and many more escort the ship for two hours. The panels close at five, and Aronnax sleeps as the Nautilus runs through the Black Current.

title: An Invitation in Writing
summary: Nemo disappears for days while the chief officer repeats a strange phrase on the platform each morning. Then a written note invites Aronnax and his companions to hunt in Nemo's forests on Crespo Island, and Nemo explains that the forests are underwater.
details: For days Captain Nemo does not appear. Aronnax studies the lounge's shells and pressed seaweeds, dresses in clothes woven from fan-mussel filaments, and begins his diary on paper made from eelgrass. Each morning, when the ship surfaces for air, the chief officer scans the horizon with a spyglass and calls down the hatch the same unintelligible phrase: "Nautron respoc lorni virch."

On November 16 Aronnax finds a note in an old-fashioned hand. Captain Nemo invites him and his companions to hunt the next morning in his forests on Crespo Island. Ned is delighted at the thought of solid ground, fresh venison and a chance to plan an escape. Aronnax finds Crespo on the map, a tiny rock in the north Pacific, and notes that Nemo only seems to visit desert islands.

Next morning Nemo, saying nothing of his eight-day absence, explains over breakfast that his forests are underwater. Aronnax briefly thinks he has gone mad. Nemo describes the gear that makes the trip possible: a Rouquayrol air tank refined to supply nine or ten hours of air under a copper helmet, a Ruhmkorff electric lamp at the belt, and air rifles that fire small glass capsules charged with electricity, fatal at the slightest touch. Convinced, Aronnax agrees, collects Ned and Conseil, and they go to the room where they will dress for the outing.

title: Strolling the Plains
summary: Ned refuses to put on a diving suit, but Aronnax and Conseil suit up and walk out onto the seafloor with Nemo and a powerful crewman. They cross sunlit plains of sand, beds of ooze and meadows of algae down to a depth of 100 meters, where Nemo points out the forest.
details: In the ship's arsenal and wardrobe, Ned Land learns the hunting grounds are underwater and refuses to wear a suit. Nobody forces him. Crewmen help Aronnax and Conseil into rubber suits with copper-mailed chests and lead-soled boots, and Captain Nemo and a herculean crewman suit up too. Aronnax inspects his rifle, which stores compressed air in its butt and holds some twenty electric bullets. With copper helmets screwed on and air tanks working, the four pass through a chamber that floods, and step out onto the bottom ten meters down.

Once in the water the gear loses most of its weight, and Aronnax moves freely. Sunlight reaches the bottom so strongly that he can see 100 meters. He crosses fine, mirror-like sand. Toward ten o'clock, slanting sunlight splits into rainbow colors along the edges of rocks, coral, anemones and shells. He cannot speak to Conseil through the helmets, while Nemo and his companion talk with hand signals, so Aronnax talks to himself and wastes air.

The ground changes to ooze, then to meadows of algae, with long ribbons of seaweed floating overhead. By noon the colors fade, and the floor slopes steeply down to 100 meters, where the light turns to a reddish twilight. Nemo stops and points to dark masses in the shadows: the forest of Crespo Island.

title: An Underwater Forest
summary: The party walks through the Crespo forest, goes deeper by lamplight to the foot of the island, and turns back without climbing ashore. On the way back they shoot a sea otter and an albatross and lie flat while two sharks pass over them.
details: In the forest every plant grows straight up toward the surface, and Aronnax keeps confusing plants with animals. Around one o'clock the party rests under the kelp, and the divers fall asleep. Aronnax wakes to find a meter-high sea spider about to spring at him, and Nemo's companion kills it with his rifle butt. Instead of turning back, Nemo leads them on and down to about 150 meters, where sunlight gives out and they switch on their lamps. Nemo raises his rifle several times but never fires.

At about four they reach a granite cliff: the base of Crespo Island, which is land. Nemo stops there and goes no farther. They return by a steeper route toward the surface. Nemo shoots a valuable sea otter, a rare animal whose fur would sell for a high price, and his companion brings down an albatross skimming the waves above them. In the shallows Aronnax sees their party reflected upside down on the underside of the surface.

Within sight of the Nautilus's beacon, Nemo suddenly throws Aronnax to the ground, and his companion does the same to Conseil. Two huge blue sharks glide past, glowing faintly. Their poor eyesight saves the divers. Half an hour later the party is back aboard, and an exhausted Aronnax goes to his cabin.

title: Four Thousand Leagues Under the Pacific
summary: Nemo talks about the ocean as a living thing, then mostly disappears as the Nautilus heads southeast past Hawaii and the Marquesas. In mid-December the travelers see a freshly sunk ship, the Florida, with its dead still on deck.
details: On November 18 some twenty crewmen haul in the nets. They are of several nationalities, all with European features, and speak only their strange language among themselves. Captain Nemo, seemingly half to himself, praises the ocean's circulation, its salts and its tiny animals, and imagines free underwater towns. Then he breaks off, perhaps at the thought of a tyrant. He asks Aronnax about known ocean depths and promises to show him deeper.

After that Nemo is rarely seen. The chief officer marks their position on the chart each day. Conseil has told Ned about the undersea walk, and Ned is sorry he missed it. The lounge panels open for hours almost daily. The ship crosses the Tropic of Cancer, passes Hawaii on November 27 after 4,860 leagues, crosses the equator on December 1 and sights Nuku Hiva in the Marquesas. On December 9–10 it runs for hours through a school of millions of migrating squid.

On December 11 the Nautilus is lying still 1,000 meters down when Conseil calls Aronnax to the window. A three-master hangs in the water, sinking, its masts cut away. Four sailors are lashed to the deck, one still at the wheel. A young woman is halfway out of a skylight, holding her child above her head. Sharks are already closing in. As the Nautilus circles, Aronnax reads the name on the stern: the Florida, of Sunderland, England.

title: Vanikoro
summary: The Nautilus crosses the South Pacific to Vanikoro, where the explorer La Pérouse's ships were wrecked. Nemo shows Aronnax the wreckage and reveals what became of the last survivors, with proof he found himself.
details: The Nautilus passes the coral islands of the Tuamotus, where Aronnax studies how coral polyps build reefs and atolls. When he says these islands may one day form a new continent, Nemo replies coldly that the earth needs new men, not new continents. The ship goes on past Tahiti, Tonga, Samoa and Fiji, where the crew feast on oysters, and through the New Hebrides at Christmas, which Ned misses keenly.

On December 27 Nemo reappears and names their position: Vanikoro, where the French navigator the Count de La Pérouse lost his two ships, the Compass and the Astrolabe, in the 1780s. At Nemo's request Aronnax recounts what is known. D'Entrecasteaux searched in vain. Captain Peter Dillon found the first relics in 1827. Dumont d'Urville raised anchors and cannon from the reef and put up a monument. The natives said the survivors built a smaller boat and sailed away, and no one knows where it was lost.

Through the lounge windows Nemo shows Aronnax coral-covered cannon, anchors and other wreckage. Then he tells him the rest: the survivors sailed for the Solomon Islands and died with all hands on the west coast of the main island. As proof he produces a tin box stamped with the arms of France. It holds La Pérouse's naval orders, with notes in the hand of King Louis XVI. Nemo calls this a fine death for a seaman, and hopes he and his companions will rest in no grave but a coral one.

title: The Torres Strait
summary: After New Year, the Nautilus threads the reefs of the Torres Strait and runs aground off Gueboroa Island. Nemo calmly waits for the full-moon tide and lets the three companions go ashore in the skiff.
details: On January 1, 1868, Conseil wishes Aronnax a happy new year. He says Ned longs for meat, bread, wine and escape, while he himself is happy to stay and see everything, so one of the two will be pleased whatever happens. The ship skirts the Great Barrier Reef, and Nemo announces they will reach the Indian Ocean through the Torres Strait, the narrow, reef-choked passage between Australia and New Guinea. Ned is glad: the route brings them nearer European seas.

With Nemo apparently steering, the Nautilus winds between the reefs on the surface. Ned says one brush with the coral would tear the hull apart. Near Gueboroa Island it strikes a reef and sticks fast at high tide. Nemo calls it "an incident," not an accident, and makes clear that nothing will make him set foot on land again. In five days the full moon will raise the tide enough to float them off, he says.

Ned thinks the ship is finished and wants to slip away, but Aronnax says escaping near New Guinea would be madness. Ned and Conseil beg for a trip ashore, and to Aronnax's surprise Nemo grants it at once and without asking for a promise to come back. On January 5, armed with rifles and axes, the three row the skiff through the reefs, Ned dreaming aloud of venison, and land on Gueboroa's beach.

title: Some Days Ashore
summary: On Gueboroa Island the three gather coconuts, breadfruit, bananas and sago and, on a second day, hunt pigeons, a bird of paradise, a wild pig and kangaroos. As they feast on the beach and talk of never going back, a stone lands at their feet.
details: On the first day Ned cracks coconuts and roasts breadfruit, which tastes like soft bread with a flavor of artichoke. He plans to ferment the pulp so it will keep aboard. The three gather bananas, jackfruit, mangoes, pineapples, palm cabbages, beans and yams, and Ned fells sago palms for their starchy flour. They return to a silent Nautilus where nobody appears.

On January 6 they go back. Wary kingfishers suggest that people visit the island often. Aronnax longs for a bird of paradise, but they waste their ammunition firing at the birds in flight. Conseil shoots a pigeon and a ringdove for lunch, then catches a rare "great emerald" bird of paradise by hand, because it is drunk on nutmeg. Aronnax explains how islanders fake these birds for European collectors. Ned finally gets his red meat: a wild pig, then a dozen small kangaroos.

At six they cook pork cutlets on the beach and feast with fruit, sago, breadfruit and fermented coconut liquor. Somewhat tipsy, Conseil wonders aloud about not returning to the Nautilus that evening, and Ned about never returning. At that moment a stone whizzes out of the forest and lands at their feet.

title: The Lightning Bolts of Captain Nemo
summary: Papuan islanders drive the three back to the ship and then surround the stranded Nautilus in growing numbers. Nemo is unconcerned, and when the hatches open at high tide, an electrified railing throws back the boarders as the ship floats free on time.
details: About twenty islanders with bows and slings attack, and the three escape in the skiff, Ned clutching his pig and kangaroos, with a hundred islanders wading after them. Aboard, they find Nemo lost in playing the organ. Unimpressed by the word "savages," he asks whether these people are any worse than men elsewhere and says the Nautilus has nothing to fear from them. Fires burn on the beach all night.

On January 8 some 500 or 600 islanders gather, crossing the exposed coral at low tide to come near the ship. Aronnax and Conseil dredge for shells, and Aronnax finds a rare treasure: an olive shell that coils the "wrong" way, left-handed. A sling stone shatters it in Conseil's hands. Conseil fires back and breaks an amulet bracelet on the thrower's arm. Aronnax tells him a shell is not worth a human life. Then dugout canoes surround the ship and arrows rain down.

Nemo, busy with calculations, has the hatches closed and says he wants no Papuan to die because of his visit. He praises Dumont d'Urville, who was nearly wrecked in this same strait, but answers icily when Aronnax says the Nautilus has run aground like d'Urville's ships. It will float off, he says, tomorrow at 2:40. That night the islanders stamp across the platform. Next afternoon the crew open the hatches. Each islander who grabs the companionway railing is hurled back in terror, and so is Ned, who cries that he has been struck by lightning. The railing is charged with the ship's electricity. At 2:40 exactly the tide lifts the Nautilus off and it leaves the Torres Strait.

title: “Aegri Somnia”
summary: The Nautilus heads west past Timor into the Indian Ocean while Nemo runs experiments on sea temperature and density. On January 18 something on the horizon throws him into a rage. The three companions are locked in their old cell and drugged to sleep.
details: The ship races west past Timor and into the open Indian Ocean. Nemo takes the Nautilus as deep as 10,000 meters to measure water temperatures himself and finds a constant 4.5 degrees centigrade at 1,000 meters. Aronnax wonders who these findings are for, since they seem bound to die with Nemo. When Nemo lists the densities of different seas, he mentions the Mediterranean, the Ionian and the Adriatic, and Aronnax concludes the ship does visit European waters.

On January 16, drifting with its beacon off, the Nautilus enters a dazzling stretch of phosphorescent water, alive with tiny glowing animals, where porpoises and sailfish play. Aronnax notes how the three have grown used to the life aboard, "at home in our shell" like snails.

On January 18, in rough weather, the chief officer calls out a different phrase. Nemo examines the horizon with growing tension and argues with his excited officer, then orders more speed. When Aronnax raises his own telescope, Nemo snatches it away, his face twisted with hatred. He is staring at the horizon, not at Aronnax. Invoking one of their agreements, he has the three companions locked in the cell where they spent their first night. After lunch the light goes out, and all three fall into a drugged sleep. Before he goes under, Aronnax hears the hatches close and feels the ship dive.

title: The Coral Realm
summary: Aronnax wakes free in his cabin, and a haggard Nemo asks him to treat a crewman with a terrible head wound, who dies in the night. The next day the three companions follow Nemo and his crew to a coral forest on the seafloor and watch the man's burial in a hidden cemetery.
details: Aronnax wakes in his own stateroom, free, with no memory of the night. Ned and Conseil know no more than he does. In the afternoon Nemo appears, exhausted and red-eyed, and asks whether Aronnax is a physician. He is, and Nemo takes him to a cabin near the crew's quarters. There a man of about forty, with English features, lies with his skull smashed open. Nemo says that in a collision an engine lever cracked, and this man threw himself in front of the chief officer to take the blow. A brother dies for his brother, Nemo says; that is the law on board. Aronnax says the man will be dead in two hours, and Nemo weeps. That night Aronnax hears something like a funeral chant.

In the morning Nemo invites the three on an undersea walk, and this time Ned comes too. With a dozen crewmen they walk into a coral realm: thickets of precious red coral whose polyps pull back at a touch, then dark galleries that slope down to about 300 meters, the depth at which coral stops growing, where the coral rises like a huge stone forest.

In a clearing stands a cross of coral among low mounds laid out by human hands. Four crewmen carry an oblong bundle. Aronnax realizes this is a cemetery, and they have brought the dead man's body. A grave is dug, the body, wrapped in fan-mussel cloth, is lowered in, and Nemo and his men kneel in prayer and farewell. Back on the platform Nemo, holding back sobs, says their dead lie here forgotten by the world but not by them, and the coral will seal them in. When Aronnax says at least the dead are safe from sharks, Nemo answers: "of sharks and men!"
